metadata.title: Original-ball paths in Teichmüller space: an elementary corollary of Lenzhen–Rafi
metadata.description:
An explicitly expository original-ball path corollary of Lenzhen–Rafi’s established uniform quasiconvexity theorem. For each fixed closed oriented surface of genus at least two, every pair of points in any original closed half-log Teichmüller ball has a continuous rectifiable path inside that same ball with length at most its ambient distance plus 4c_g. One finite topology-dependent c_g works for all centers, radii and pairs. Radial endpoint retreat followed by a minimizing segment gives the deduction and an affirmative derivation of Farb’s Question 3.5 from prior geometry.

All substantive Teichmüller estimates are credited to Lenzhen–Rafi. Historical priority for the elementary lemma and exact corollary is unestablished; no new substantive theorem, worldwide firstness, current openness, numerical or genus-uniform constant, or optimal Teichmüller bound is claimed. Kerckhoff’s formula and Fortier Bourque–Rafi’s metric and nonconvexity interfaces are credited. Petyt–Zalloum’s 2024/2026 dual wall-space almost convexity uses a different metric, with no comparison of numerical constants. A bounded priority audit does not certify absence of prior work.

The deposit includes the full proof, TeX source, scope supplement, byte-preserved theoretical original and authored independent adversarial mathematical and source audits. No original executable was submitted; these are written verification materials, not a computational or proof-assistant certificate. Third-party paper bodies are omitted. AI tools were used extensively in deriving, verifying, adversarial review, source auditing and preparation. This is an unrefereed expository preprint; conventional human peer review and journal acceptance are not claimed.
references: B. Farb, Some problems on mapping class groups and moduli space, in Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics (2006), pp. 24–25, Question 3.5. https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~farb/papers/mcgbook.pdf

A. Lenzhen and K. Rafi, Length of a curve is quasi-convex along a Teichmüller geodesic, J. Differential Geom. 88 (2011), 267–295, Theorems C, 15 and 17. https://www.math.toronto.edu/rafi/Papers/Convexity.pdf
S. P. Kerckhoff, The asymptotic geometry of Teichmüller space, Topology 19 (1980), 23–41. https://doi.org/10.1016/0040-9383(80)90029-4
M. Fortier Bourque and K. Rafi, Non-convex balls in the Teichmüller metric, J. Differential Geom. 110 (2018), 379–412; arXiv:1606.05170v3 (2017). https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.05170v3
